import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.16

by F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III

Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?

In (G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III, *Math. Z.* **153** (1977), 117–134) it
is proved that every countable group which is locally linear of bounded degree can be
embedded in a finitely presented group with solvable word problem.

A group is *linear of degree $n$* if it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for
some field $F$ (of any characteristic), and *locally linear* if every finitely generated
subgroup is linear (the degree $n$ and the field $F$ may depend on the subgroup). It is
*locally linear of bounded degree* if a single degree $n$ works for all finitely generated
subgroups (the field may still vary). A group is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_k \rangle$ for finitely many generators and
relators; such a presentation has *solvable word problem* if the set of words in the
generators and their inverses that represent the identity is decidable.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 5.16
* G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III, *Infinitely generated subgroups of
  finitely presented groups. I*, Math. Z. **153** (1977), 117–134
-/
namespace Kourovka.«5.16»
universe u

blocks.code:
def IsLinearOfDegree (G : Type u) [Group G] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (F : Type u) (_ : Field F) (φ : G →* GL (Fin n) F), Function.Injective φ
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` is *linear of degree `n`* if it embeds in the general linear group
$\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$.

The field is taken in the same universe as `G`. This loses no generality: the matrix entries of
the image of `G` generate a subfield of cardinality at most $\max(|G|, \aleph_0)$, and `G` also
embeds in $\mathrm{GL}_n$ of this subfield.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup / GL (Fin n) F, LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup — these are the target groups but there is no 'is linear' predicate on abstract groups.
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.16».IsLinearOfDegree
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has GL (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup) but no predicate 'G is (isomorphic to) a linear group of degree n over some field'.

blocks.name: IsLinearOfDegree
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` is *linear of degree `n`* if it embeds in the general linear group
$\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$.

The field is taken in the same universe as `G`. This loses no generality: the matrix entries of
the image of `G` generate a subfield of cardinality at most $\max(|G|, \aleph_0)$, and `G` also
embeds in $\mathrm{GL}_n$ of this subfield. -/
def IsLinearOfDegree (G : Type u) [Group G] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (F : Type u) (_ : Field F) (φ : G →* GL (Fin n) F), Function.Injective φ

blocks.code:
def IsLocallyLinear (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → ∃ n : ℕ, IsLinearOfDegree H n
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` is *locally linear* if every finitely generated subgroup of `G` is linear
(of some degree, over some field, both possibly depending on the subgroup).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.FG / Group.FG (used to express 'finitely generated subgroup').
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.16».IsLocallyLinear
justification.why_needed: No notion of locally linear group in Mathlib or the repo (SimpleGraph.LocallyLinear in the repo is an unrelated graph notion).

blocks.name: IsLocallyLinear
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` is *locally linear* if every finitely generated subgroup of `G` is linear
(of some degree, over some field, both possibly depending on the subgroup). -/
def IsLocallyLinear (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → ∃ n : ℕ, IsLinearOfDegree H n

blocks.code:
def IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsLinearOfDegree H n
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` is *locally linear of bounded degree* if there is an `n` such that every
finitely generated subgroup of `G` is linear of degree `n` (over some field, possibly depending
on the subgroup). Since $\mathrm{GL}_m(F)$ embeds in $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for $m \le n$, this is
the same as bounding the degrees of the finitely generated subgroups by `n`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsLocallyLinear with the ∃ n pulled outside the ∀ H.
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.16».IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree
justification.why_needed: Needed for the bounded-degree variant: a single degree n for all finitely generated subgroups.

blocks.name: IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` is *locally linear of bounded degree* if there is an `n` such that every
finitely generated subgroup of `G` is linear of degree `n` (over some field, possibly depending
on the subgroup). Since $\mathrm{GL}_m(F)$ embeds in $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for $m \le n$, this is
the same as bounding the degrees of the finitely generated subgroups by `n`. -/
def IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsLinearOfDegree H n

blocks.code:
def IsFinitelyPresented (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* PresentedGroup rels)
blocks.docstring:
A group `P` is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite
set `rels` of relators in the free group on finitely many generators `Fin n`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«5.16».IsFinitelyPresented
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has PresentedGroup and Group.FG but no predicate for finitely presented groups (Module.FinitePresentation / Algebra.FinitePresentation are for modules/algebras only).

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented
blocks.text:
/-- A group `P` is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite
set `rels` of relators in the free group on finitely many generators `Fin n`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

blocks.code:
def PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) => PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1
blocks.docstring:
The presentation `⟨Fin n | rels⟩` has *solvable word problem* if the set of words
`w : List (Fin n × Bool)` in the generators and their inverses that represent the identity of
`PresentedGroup rels` is computable (i.e. recursive).

justification.name: Kourovka.«5.16».PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem
justification.why_needed: No word-problem notion for group presentations in Mathlib; defined via ComputablePred on words List (Fin n × Bool) representing the identity in PresentedGroup rels.

blocks.name: PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem
blocks.text:
/-- The presentation `⟨Fin n | rels⟩` has *solvable word problem* if the set of words
`w : List (Fin n × Bool)` in the generators and their inverses that represent the identity of
`PresentedGroup rels` is computable (i.e. recursive). -/
def PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) => PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

blocks.docstring:
A group `P` is *finitely presented with solvable word problem* if it has a finite
presentation whose word problem is solvable. (Solvability of the word problem does not depend
on the choice of finite presentation.)

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsFinitelyPresented (same file) conjoined with PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem for the same presentation.
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.16».IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem
justification.why_needed: Conclusion of the Baumslag–Cannonito–Miller theorem: existence of a finite presentation with solvable word problem.

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem
blocks.text:
/-- A group `P` is *finitely presented with solvable word problem* if it has a finite
presentation whose word problem is solvable. (Solvability of the word problem does not depend
on the choice of finite presentation.) -/
def IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* PresentedGroup rels) ∧
    PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem rels

theorem kourovka.«5.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G], IsLocallyLinear G →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresented P ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* P, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

theorem kourovka.«5.16».variants.bounded_degree :

blocks.docstring:
Every countable group which is locally linear of bounded degree can be embedded in a
finitely presented group with solvable word problem.

That is, if $G$ is a countable group and there is an $n$ such that every finitely generated
subgroup of $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$ (depending

claims.decomposer_note: Open yes/no question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G countable group, (∀ finitely generated subgroup H of G, ∃ field F and n, H embeds in GL_n(F)) → ∃ finitely presented group P with an injective hom G →* P); 'locally linear' means every finitely generated subgroup is linear where the degree n and the field F may vary with the subgroup (any characteristic), 'countable' includes finite groups, and 'finitely presented' has no Mathlib predicate so it must be defined (e.g. ∃ n and a finite set of relators in FreeGroup (Fin n) with G ≃* PresentedGroup rels); implicitly this includes the Higman-necessary condition that G be recursively presented, which is part of what is open.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state this slot with the same (faithful) shape; c03 chosen for its complete docstrings and API/test lemmas. Final uses c03's declaration verbatim with the field quantified in G's universe (c06's approach) instead of hard-coded `Type` — WLOG either way. Locally linear = every Subgroup.FG subgroup embeds in GL (Fin n) F with n and field F depending on the subgroup; Countable includes finite; finitely presented = ≃* PresentedGroup rels on Fin n generators with rels.Finite; embedding = injective MonoidHom; answer(True) is the positive answer. No recursive-presentability hypothesis was added (the notebook's question is literal, and c03/c06 correctly object to the table's 'Higman-necessary' remark).

claims.decomposer_note: Known theorem (Baumslag–Cannonito–Miller, Math. Z. 153 (1977)), so category research solved: the special case where a single degree n works for all finitely generated subgroups (the field may still vary — check the paper for whether the field is also fixed) with the stronger conclusion 'finitely presented with solvable word problem'; the solvable-word-problem clause needs a computability notion absent from Mathlib, so a formalizer may have to state only the finitely-presented embedding (which still implies the primary question's conclusion for this case) and document the omission.
claims.reviewer_why: Bounded degree = ∃ n, every f.g. subgroup embeds in GL_n(F) for some field F depending on the subgroup (literal notebook reading; equivalent to a fixed field by Mal'cev's local theorem, so the statement follows from BCM 1977 under either reading). Conclusion includes the solvable-word-problem clause via Mathlib's ComputablePred on words List (Fin n × Bool) mapping to 1 in PresentedGroup rels, for some finite presentation (presentation-independence makes ∃ correct). c01/c08 omitted this clause claiming Mathlib lacks the notion; that is incorrect (ComputablePred is genuine partial-recursive computability and is already used in Paper/BranchingVAS.lean), so c02–c07's stronger, faithful statement is preferred. c04's custom evalWord and c06/c07's generating-set formulation are also correct but c03's is closest to the classical 'finitely presented with solvable word problem'. Category research solved, AMS 3 20.

decomposition_objections.text: Minor: the note on the primary slot says the statement 'implicitly includes the Higman-necessary condition that G be recursively presented'. For infinitely generated countable groups, recursive presentability is not a necessary condition for embeddability in a finitely presented group (e.g. every subgroup of ℚ, including non-recursively-presentable ones, embeds in a finitely presented group because ℚ does), so no such hypothesis was added; the slot is stated literally as in the notebook. Also, the note for the variant says the solvable-word-problem clause needs a computability notion absent from Mathlib; in fact Mathlib's ComputablePred suffices (and is already used in FormalConjectures/Paper/BranchingVAS.lean), so the clause was included rather than omitted.

namespace Kourovka.«5.16»

universe u

/-- A group `G` is *linear of degree `n`* if it embeds in the general linear group
$\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$.

The field is taken in the same universe as `G`. This loses no generality: the matrix entries of
the image of `G` generate a subfield of cardinality at most $\max(|G|, \aleph_0)$, and `G` also
embeds in $\mathrm{GL}_n$ of this subfield. -/
def IsLinearOfDegree (G : Type u) [Group G] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (F : Type u) (_ : Field F) (φ : G →* GL (Fin n) F), Function.Injective φ

/-- A group `G` is *locally linear* if every finitely generated subgroup of `G` is linear
(of some degree, over some field, both possibly depending on the subgroup). -/
def IsLocallyLinear (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → ∃ n : ℕ, IsLinearOfDegree H n

/-- A group `G` is *locally linear of bounded degree* if there is an `n` such that every
finitely generated subgroup of `G` is linear of degree `n` (over some field, possibly depending
on the subgroup). Since $\mathrm{GL}_m(F)$ embeds in $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for $m \le n$, this is
the same as bounding the degrees of the finitely generated subgroups by `n`. -/
def IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsLinearOfDegree H n

/-- A group `P` is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite
set `rels` of relators in the free group on finitely many generators `Fin n`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- The presentation `⟨Fin n | rels⟩` has *solvable word problem* if the set of words
`w : List (Fin n × Bool)` in the generators and their inverses that represent the identity of
`PresentedGroup rels` is computable (i.e. recursive). -/
def PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) => PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- A group `P` is *finitely presented with solvable word problem* if it has a finite
presentation whose word problem is solvable. (Solvability of the word problem does not depend
on the choice of finite presentation.) -/
def IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* PresentedGroup rels) ∧
    PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem rels

/--
Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?

That is, if $G$ is a countable group all of whose finitely generated subgroups are linear
(each over some field and of some degree), does there exist a finitely presented group $P$
and an injective group homomorphism $G \to P$? Here countable includes finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G], IsLocallyLinear G →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresented P ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* P, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

/--
Every countable group which is locally linear of bounded degree can be embedded in a
finitely presented group with solvable word problem.

That is, if $G$ is a countable group and there is an $n$ such that every finitely generated
subgroup of $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$ (depending
on the subgroup), then there is a finitely presented group $P$ with solvable word problem and an
injective group homomorphism $G \to P$.

This is the theorem of G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito and C. F. Miller III,
*Math. Z.* **153** (1977), 117–134, cited in the statement of Problem 5.16.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16».variants.bounded_degree :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G], IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree G →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem P ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* P, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

/-- The general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ is linear of degree `n`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLinearOfDegree_generalLinearGroup (n : ℕ) (F : Type u) [Field F] :
    IsLinearOfDegree (GL (Fin n) F) n :=
  ⟨F, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id _, fun _ _ h => h⟩

/-- A subgroup of a linear group of degree `n` is linear of degree `n`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLinearOfDegree.subgroup {G : Type u} [Group G] {n : ℕ} (h : IsLinearOfDegree G n)
    (H : Subgroup G) : IsLinearOfDegree H n := by
  obtain ⟨F, _, φ, hφ⟩ := h
  exact ⟨F, inferInstance, φ.comp H.subtype, hφ.comp Subtype.val_injective⟩

/-- A linear group is locally linear of bounded degree. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLinearOfDegree.isLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree {G : Type u} [Group G] {n : ℕ}
    (h : IsLinearOfDegree G n) : IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree G :=
  ⟨n, fun H _ => h.subgroup H⟩

/-- A group which is locally linear of bounded degree is locally linear. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree.isLocallyLinear {G : Type*} [Group G]
    (h : IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree G) : IsLocallyLinear G :=
  fun H hH => h.elim fun n hn => ⟨n, hn H hH⟩

/-- A group given by a finite presentation is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} {rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))}
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨n, rels, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- A finitely presented group with solvable word problem is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem.isFinitelyPresented {P : Type*} [Group P]
    (h : IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem P) : IsFinitelyPresented P :=
  h.elim fun n ⟨rels, hfin, he, _⟩ => ⟨n, rels, hfin, he⟩

/-- The empty presentation of the trivial group has solvable word problem. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem trivialPresentation_hasSolvableWordProblem :
    PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem (∅ : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0))) :=
  ComputablePred.of_eq (p := fun _ => True) ⟨inferInstance, by simpa using Computable.const true⟩
    fun w => ⟨fun _ => by rw [Subsingleton.elim (FreeGroup.mk w) 1, map_one], fun _ => trivial⟩

end Kourovka.«5.16»

items: 'Linear' means embeddable in GL_n(F) for a field F (commutative), with F : Type. Restricting F to universe 0 loses no generality: the matrix entries of the image of a countable group generate a countable subfield, which is equivalent to a type in Type. Similarly G : Type and P : Type are WLOG since G is countable and finitely presented groups are countable.

'Locally linear' is formalized as: every finitely generated subgroup H (H.FG) is linear, with the degree n and the field F allowed to depend on H (any characteristic). 'Locally linear of bounded degree' fixes one n for all f.g. subgroups but lets the field vary. This is the literal reading of the notebook text ('locally linear' + 'of bounded degree'); I could not access the Baumslag–Cannonito–Miller paper (no network) to confirm whether they additionally fix the field. If the paper fixes the field, the variant as stated is stronger than the cited theorem (but still implied by the standard reading of the abstract). Note: 'degree exactly n' vs 'degree ≤ n' are equivalent since GL_m(F) embeds in GL_n(F) for m ≤ n.
'Finitely presented' is ∃ n and a finite set rels ⊆ FreeGroup (Fin n) with P ≃* PresentedGroup rels (Nonempty of the MulEquiv type).

'Solvable word problem' is formalized for a specific finite presentation as ComputablePred (Mathlib's computability notion, w.r.t. the Primcodable encoding of List (Fin n × Bool)) of the set of words representing 1 in PresentedGroup rels. Solvability is independent of the chosen finite presentation, so requiring it for some finite presentation is equivalent to the standard notion.
Countable G includes finite groups, matching group-theoretic usage of 'countable'.

The decomposition notes say recursive presentability of G is 'Higman-necessary'; this is not imposed as a hypothesis (the question is stated for all countable locally linear groups, as in the notebook). Note that for infinitely generated countable groups recursive presentability is not literally necessary (e.g. every subgroup of ℚ embeds in a finitely presented group), so the literal statement is the right one.

Added short API/test lemmas (with proofs) for the bespoke definitions as CONTRIBUTING.md requests; the generic definitions (IsLinearOfDegree, IsFinitelyPresented, word problem) would ideally live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib, but the task restricts output to the single problem file.

File compiles via `lake env lean` with only the two 'declaration uses sorry' warnings and builds as a module with `lake --wfail build`. Ambiguities: 'locally linear of bounded degree' could mean fixed field or varying field; the varying-field reading is used (literal, and equivalent via Mal'cev). 'Linear' is over a (commutative) field, the standard meaning. The table's suggestion that the word-problem clause needs a computability notion absent from Mathlib is inaccurate — ComputablePred suffices — so the clause was kept rather than omitted. The primary question was stated literally without any recursive-presentability hypothesis.
